q: The Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction is used to study bifurcation from a known solution u₀ of F(u,λ) = 0 when the Fréchet derivative D_uF(u₀,λ₀) has a nontrivial kernel. It splits the equation into:
opts: An equation in the image of D_uF (solvable by implicit function theorem) and a finite-dimensional bifurcation equation in the kernel
exp: Lyapunov-Schmidt: project onto Im(L) and Ker(L*). The Im(L) component is solved by IFT (giving u as a function of the kernel component v and λ); the Ker(L*) component gives the bifurcation equation G(v,λ) = 0, which is finite-dimensional.
